question: What numerical distinctions are made for self-manifested and great-established cases?
premises: A self-manifested case is associated with one thousand and one.
Great ones are associated with five hundred.
inference: The self-manifested case involves one thousand and one, while that of the great ones involves five hundred.
uncertainties: The units being counted are not explicitly named in this verse.
plain_english: In the self-manifested case there are one thousand and one; by the great ones, five hundred.
